text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris. The presence of flaccid blisters on the forearm with confirmed acantholysis, combined with widespread mucosal involvement (buccal, gingival, vulvar) and negative HSV/VZV serologies, is clinically diagnostic for Pemphigus Vulgaris. The negative viral workup and specific histological finding of acantholysis rule out herpes and varicella zoster etiologies.
